# Exact epimorphism counting for bounded-generator solvable A-group targets

**Theorem.** Fix a positive integer \(d\). Given Cayley tables for any finite group \(G\) and any finite solvable group \(H\) generated by at most \(d\) elements and having abelian Sylow subgroups, one can list all epimorphisms \(G\twoheadrightarrow H\) in deterministic polynomial bit time. The number of epimorphisms is at most \(|H|\,|G/G^{(\ell)}|^d\), where \(\ell\) is the derived length of \(H\) and \(G^{(i)}\) denotes the \(i\)-th derived subgroup. In particular, the source has no solvability, generation or Sylow promise.

The proof uses the abelian-layer Smith lift from [Four algebraic algorithms](https://github.com/Dugongue/MathProofs/blob/main/FourAlgebraicAlgorithms/PROOF.md), the compatible extension equations from [Simultaneous isomorphism of abelian extensions](https://github.com/Dugongue/MathProofs/blob/main/AbelianExtensionLinearization/PROOF.md), and the coprime layer viewpoint in [Group, graph, and tensor isomorphism crossovers](https://github.com/Dugongue/MathProofs/blob/main/GroupGraphTensorCrossovers/PROOF.md). Skresanov's split last-derived subgroup construction brings these together for solvable groups with abelian Sylows, including those with no Sylow tower. This proves an epimorphism analogue of the bounded-generator part of Skresanov's setting and resolves the bounded-generator target cases of the Sylow-tower clause in [Grochow–Srivastava–Thakkar Open Question 3(4)](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.07429v1#S7), beyond their class on both sides of the map. It also covers the solvable A-group part of the bounded-generator target clause in their Question 3(2), with search and exact counting as in Question 2.

## 1. A coprime module count

Let \(L\) be a finite group of order prime to \(p\), and let \(A,B\) be finite abelian \(p\)-groups with \(L\)-actions. If \(A\) is generated by \(d\) elements as an \(L\)-module, then

\[
|\operatorname{Hom}_L(B,A)|\le |B|^d.
\]

The sequences for multiplication by \(p\) and for quotienting by \(pA\) show that \(A[p]\) and \(A/pA\) have the same composition factors as finite \(\mathbb Z[L]\)-modules. Both are semisimple \(\mathbb F_p[L]\)-modules by Maschke's theorem, hence are isomorphic. The generator hypothesis makes \(A/pA\) a quotient of \(\mathbb F_p[L]^d\). The quotient splits, so \(A[p]\) embeds in that regular module. For elementary abelian \(C\), evaluation of an equivariant map to the regular module at the identity-coordinate identifies those maps with arbitrary linear forms \(C\to\mathbb F_p\). Indeed, the other coordinates are obtained by translating this functional by elements of \(L\). Therefore \(|\operatorname{Hom}_L(C,A[p])|\le |C|^d\). For general \(B\), restriction from \(B\) to \(pB\) has fibers of size at most \(|\operatorname{Hom}_L(B/pB,A[p])|\). Induction proves the bound.

## 2. Charging lifts to one derived section of the source

Suppose \(H\) has derived length \(i\ge2\), let \(A=H^{(i-1)}\), and put \(Q=H/A\). The proof of [Skresanov, Lemma 5.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.26748v2#S5) gives a complement to the full last nontrivial derived subgroup in this setting. Specifically, its relative system normalizer complements \([H^{(i-2)},H^{(i-2)}]=A\) before the proof passes to a single primary component. Thus \(H=A\rtimes Q\). Decomposing a group generating tuple of length at most \(d\) into \(A\)-parts and \(Q\)-parts shows that the \(A\)-parts generate \(A\) as a \(Q\)-module. Every word in the tuple has \(A\)-coordinate in their module span. Consequently every primary component \(A_p\) also has at most \(d\) module generators.

Write \(E=Q^{(i-2)}\). This is abelian, and \(H^{(i-2)}=A\rtimes E\), because it maps onto \(E\) and contains \(A\). Taking commutators gives \(A=[A,E]\). Each \(p\)-element of \(Q\) centralizes \(A_p\), since together they form a \(p\)-subgroup of \(H\), and all such subgroups are abelian. It follows that \(A_p=[A_p,E_{p'}]\), where \(E_{p'}\) is the prime-to-\(p\) subgroup of the finite abelian group \(E\). The averaging projector onto \(A_p^{E_{p'}}\) annihilates every commutator difference. Hence \(A_p^{E_{p'}}=0\).

Fix an epimorphism \(\psi:G\twoheadrightarrow Q\). Every lift to \(H\) factors through \(\bar G=G/G^{(i)}\). Put \(D=G^{(i-1)}/G^{(i)}\), an abelian subgroup of \(\bar G\), and use the same symbol for the induced \(\psi\). Relative to the splitting, a lift has the form \(g\mapsto (a(g),\psi(g))\), with \(a\) a crossed homomorphism. Its restriction to \(D\) is an additive map equivariant for the conjugation action of \(\bar G\) on \(D\) and the \(\psi\)-action on \(A\). For a prime \(p\) dividing \(|A|\), an equivariant map to \(A_p\) uses only \(D_p\). It factors first through the quotient of \(D_p\) by differences \(k x-x\) for \(k\in\ker\psi\), giving a \(Q\)-module. Since all \(p\)-elements of \(Q\) act trivially on \(A_p\), factor the domain again by differences for the subgroup generated by those elements. The remaining action factors through a group of order prime to \(p\), since the killed subgroup contains a Sylow \(p\)-subgroup. Section 1 then bounds the number of choices for this primary restriction by \(|D_p|^d\). The total number of restrictions to \(D\) is at most \(|D|^d\).

Two lifts with the same restriction have difference a crossed homomorphism \(\delta\) on \(\bar G/D\) with values in \(A\). For each primary component, consider the abelian normal subgroup \(E_0=(\bar G/D)^{(i-2)}\) of \(\bar G/D\). It maps onto \(E\), so its characteristic subgroup \((E_0)_{p'}\) maps onto \(E_{p'}\). Averaging \(\delta\) on \((E_0)_{p'}\) gives \(b\in A_p\) with \(\delta(x)=b-xb\) there. Subtract this principal crossed homomorphism. The new one vanishes on that normal subgroup. Its value on any \(g\) is fixed by the subgroup, by expanding \(xg=g(g^{-1}xg)\) in the cocycle equation. As the fixed space is zero, the new cocycle vanishes everywhere. There are at most \(|A_p|\) choices for the original primary difference and hence at most \(|A|\) lifts over each restriction. This bounds **all** homomorphism lifts over the fixed onto \(\psi\), including lifts that fail to be onto \(H\), by

\[
 |A|\,|G^{(i-1)}/G^{(i)}|^d.
\]

For an abelian target of generator number at most \(d\), the bound \(|G/G'|^d\) on all homomorphisms follows by decomposing the target into at most \(d\) cyclic factors. For a cyclic target, the number of homomorphisms from a finite abelian group is at most the order of that group by the cyclic-factor formula. Iterating the last-derived lift along \(H/H^{(i)}\) multiplies the orders of the target layers, yielding \(|H|\), and multiplies the orders of the corresponding derived source sections, yielding \(|G/G^{(\ell)}|\). It also gives the same bound with \(H/H^{(i)}\) and \(G/G^{(i)}\) at every intermediate stage, even when counting the failed surjectivity candidates for that stage.

## 3. Deterministic execution from tables

Derived subgroups, normal closures, quotients, and set sections are computable by product and inverse closure and table scans. The complement from Section 2 is needed for the counting argument. To implement the algorithm one can use any set section \(s:Q\to H\). Write \(c(q,r)=s(q)s(r)s(qr)^{-1}\in A\), and write the conjugation action of \(q\) on \(A\) additively. The possible lifts of \(\psi\) are precisely the assignments in \(A^{|G|}\) satisfying

\[
 a_{gu}=a_g+\psi(g)a_u+c(\psi(g),\psi(u))\qquad(g,u\in G).
\]

The abelian target at the first stage is the same system with trivial quotient. For the computations, present \(A\) additively with one generator per element and one relation per table product. Smith normal form gives cyclic coordinates and the coordinate vector of each element. Conjugation actions are obtained by applying table conjugation to cyclic generators. Each displayed constraint is an affine congruence system in the cyclic coordinates. Add the row moduli as columns to the integer coefficient matrix. The constant vector lies in that column lattice exactly when the system is feasible. Polynomial-time integer Hermite or Smith normal form decides membership and can recover a solution. There are at most polynomially many coordinates, relations and coefficient bits in the explicit table sizes. [Kannan–Bachem, polynomial algorithms for Smith and Hermite normal forms](https://doi.org/10.1137/0208040)

To enumerate, order the elements of \(G\). At each step try every element of \(A\) for the next coordinate and run the same affine feasibility test with the prefix fixed. Every visited feasible prefix has a full completion. Thus the tested nodes are bounded by \(1+|A||G|\) times the number of complete lifts, with one root test when there are no lifts. At complete assignments check surjectivity on the raw table, retaining only epimorphisms for the next stage. Each map has a unique projection to the previous stage, so there are no duplicates. The bounds of Section 2 make the full algorithm polynomial for fixed \(d\). Exact counting is then just counting retained maps, and any retained map provides search.

## 4. Extension to targets with abelian kernels

**Corollary.** Exact epimorphism counting and search remain in deterministic polynomial time, for arbitrary source and a \(d\)-generated target \(H\), if \(H\) admits an abelian normal subgroup \(N\) for which \(H/N\) is a solvable A-group. The subgroup need not be supplied. This class includes every bounded-generator metabelian target and every bounded-generator solvable A-group target.

Let \(\Lambda(H)\) be the normal closure of commutators \([x,y]\) with \(\langle x,y\rangle\) of prime-power order. In any quotient with abelian Sylow subgroups these commutators vanish. Conversely, any Sylow subgroup of \(H/\Lambda(H)\) is the image of a Sylow subgroup of \(H\). All commutators within the latter were killed, so the former is abelian. Thus the target condition is equivalent to solvability of \(H\) and abelianness of \(\Lambda(H)\). The latter can be found by scanning pairs of elements and taking subgroup and normal closure. A metabelian \(H\) qualifies because \(\Lambda(H)\le H'\). A solvable A-group qualifies because \(\Lambda(H)=1\).

Set \(N=\Lambda(H)\), and use the theorem to list all epimorphisms \(\psi:G\twoheadrightarrow H/N\). Select a generating tuple \((h_1,\ldots,h_d)\) of \(H\), padding with identities as needed. At each \(\psi\) enumerate all \(d\)-tuples \((g_1,\ldots,g_d)\) in \(G\) with the prescribed quotient images, and count the affine solutions with \(f(g_j)=h_j\). As in the bounded-generator metabelian proof, a nonempty affine solution set has size \(|N|^{|G|}/|\operatorname{im} M|\) for its congruence homomorphism \(M\). Smith form computes the image order by the index of the image lattice in the output coordinate lattice. All those lifts are onto, and each epi occurs exactly \((|G|/|H|)^d\) times, one choice of preimage per fixed target generator. First reject if \(|H|\nmid|G|\). The number of enumerated systems is polynomial, and one feasible system gives a witness. This argument allows nonsplit abelian kernels and possibly too many complete lifts of the final layer to enumerate individually.

## 5. Central extensions with no generator bound on the target

**Theorem.** Suppose \(N\le Z(H)\) and \(H/N\) is a solvable A-group generated by at most \(d\) elements. For arbitrary source \(G\), the count of all epimorphisms \(G\twoheadrightarrow H\) and a witness when there is one are computable deterministically in polynomial bit time for fixed \(d\). The orders, rank and exponent of \(N\), and the generator number of \(H\), are unrestricted. The central subgroup may be supplied, or one may take \(N=Z(H)\) and test the condition on the resulting quotient directly from the table. This generalizes the bounded-central-quotient case of [Exact group epimorphism counting by central lifts and commutator maps](https://github.com/Dugongue/MathProofs/blob/main/GroupEpimorphismCounting/PROOF.md).

Use the first theorem to enumerate all epimorphisms \(\psi:G\twoheadrightarrow Q=H/N\). For each \(\psi\), let \(K=\ker\psi\). Obtain a feasible homomorphism lift \(f_0:G\to H\) by the Smith method above or skip the projection if no lift exists. Because \(N\) is central, all other lifts are uniquely \(f(g)=f_0(g)\alpha(g)\), with \(\alpha\in\operatorname{Hom}(G,N)\). A lift is onto exactly when \(f(K)=N\). The restriction to \(K\) always lands in \(N\), and if its image contains \(N\) then the surjective quotient image implies surjectivity upstairs.

For each prime \(p\) of \(|N|\), write \(N_p\) as a product of cyclic groups of orders \(p^{e_j}\). Let \(V=(K_{\mathrm{ab}}/pK_{\mathrm{ab}})^*\) over \(\mathbb F_p\). The \(j\)-th row of the map \(f|_K\) modulo \(pN_p\) lies in the affine subset \(t_j+S_{e_j}\) of \(V\), where \(t_j\) is the row of \(f_0|_K\) and \(S_e\) is the image of \(\operatorname{Hom}(G_{\mathrm{ab}},C_{p^e})\) by restriction to \(K\) and reduction modulo \(p\). Each row in this affine subset has the same number of lifts, namely \(|\operatorname{Hom}(G_{\mathrm{ab}},C_{p^{e_j}})|/p^{\dim S_{e_j}}\). Coordinates of \(\alpha\) on different target cyclic factors are independent. The subspaces satisfy \(S_e\subseteq S_{e-1}\) for \(e\ge2\), by composing any homomorphism with the natural reduction of cyclic groups. A set of row choices gives a surjection onto \(N\) exactly when, for each prime \(p\), the rows are independent. Indeed a subgroup of a finite abelian \(p\)-group is the whole group if its image in the quotient by \(p\) is the whole quotient. This follows by writing the quotient by the subgroup as equal to its own multiple by \(p\), and iterating to zero. Surjectivity to all primary factors separately is enough since a subgroup of a finite abelian group splits into its primary factors.

At a fixed prime, sort the rows by decreasing \(e_j\), so their direction spaces grow. Given any already selected independent first \(j-1\) rows, let \(P\) be their span and put \(S=S_{e_j}\). The projection of \(P\) in \(V/S\) is the span of the images of \(t_1,\ldots,t_{j-1}\), because their direction spaces are contained in \(S\). Its rank \(r_j\) depends only on the known offsets. If \(t_j\) projects outside this span, every element of \(t_j+S\) extends the independent list. Otherwise the forbidden intersection \(P\cap(t_j+S)\) is a translate of \(P\cap S\), with exactly \(p^{j-1-r_j}\) elements. So the number of choices at every step depends only on the input and is \(p^{\dim S}\) or \(p^{\dim S}-p^{j-1-r_j}\), respectively. Their product, times the product of the row fiber sizes, counts exactly the onto lifts for this prime. Multiply over primes, and sum over the distinct quotient maps \(\psi\).

All the subspaces and fibers are computable from cyclic coordinates. A cyclic source factor of order \(b\) contributes \(\gcd(b,p^e)\) choices when mapping to \(C_{p^e}\). A generating list for these homomorphisms consists of one map per cyclic factor, sending its generator to a generator of the corresponding subgroup of \(C_{p^e}\). Restrict those maps to \(K\) and reduce modulo \(p\) to obtain a spanning list for \(S_e\). Here \(K\) and its abelianization are computed from the table. Rank and membership over \(\mathbb F_p\), and powers with polynomial bit length, give the exact output. For search, choose one independent row at a time whenever the product is positive. The offset itself is either a valid choice or, if it lies in the old span, adding a direction-space basis vector outside that span gives a valid choice. Express the chosen differences in the calculated spanning lists and lift each combination to an actual cyclic-coordinate homomorphism using the same list. This constructs the map \(\alpha\) and the required epimorphism.

## Scope and prior work

These are informal proofs. They give an unconditional bounded-target-generator extension of the abelian Sylow tower part of [Grochow–Srivastava–Thakkar](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.07429v1#S7), with unrestricted source. Their algorithms without a generator bound for particular coprime two-layer families are complementary. Skresanov computes isomorphisms and automorphisms on solvable A-groups. Matei–Suciu give a generalized Gaschütz recursion for epimorphism counts into solvable groups. Here the restriction to a single derived source section yields a polynomial bound at every intermediate stage. For central extensions, nested affine row spaces allow exact counting of lifts even when enumeration would exceed a polynomial bound. The general tower question without a generator bound and the general bounded-generator question remain outside these results. Publication priority for the new bounds and algorithms has not been established. [Skresanov](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26748) · [Matei–Suciu](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0405122)
